drg.description: Simple Pneumonia and Pleurisy with CC

timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 82-year-old male admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.51, creatinine 0.81-0.87, hemoglobin 13.7-13.9, platelets 218-224, sodium 124-127, wbc 6.2-7; vitals dbp 64-70, heart_rate 72-78, map 86-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 125-130, spo2 97-99, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Fluid restriction 1.2 L/day; Sodium chloride 1 g PO TID
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Hyponatremia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.82-0.87, hemoglobin 13.7-13.8, platelets 216-227, sodium 127-130, wbc 6.3-6.7; vitals dbp 65-69, heart_rate 72-78, map 85-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 124-130, spo2 97-99, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Hyponatremia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 82-year-old male, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Hyponatremia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
